faqs.q: What information do you need from us to start?
faqs.a: We send you a structured intake form covering your product or service line, current revenue and channels, competitive landscape as you see it, and growth goals. Most clients complete it in 30 to 45 minutes. If anything is missing, we proceed using secondary research and proxy benchmarks, and log every assumption explicitly in the report.

faqs.q: How is this different from hiring a consultant?
faqs.a: A consultant gives you one opinion and charges monthly. This delivers a structured, evidence-based growth roadmap with ranked moves, investment estimates, and an action plan — in 14 days, at a fixed price. Every recommendation is sourced, not just experienced. And you get the full methodology, not a black box.

faqs.q: Is this only for US-based businesses?
faqs.a: The core methodology works for any geography, but our deepest data coverage is in the US market. For US-based small and mid-size businesses, we have the strongest secondary data access and competitive intelligence. International businesses operating in the US are also a strong fit.

faqs.q: What if we already know our competitors?
faqs.a: Good — that saves time on the intake. But most businesses underestimate their competitive set. We independently identify 5–10 competitors through market research, which often surfaces indirect competitors or emerging threats that weren't on your radar. The competitive matrix is one of the most valued sections.

faqs.q: Can our agency white-label this and deliver it to our client?
faqs.a: Yes. The report is designed for white-label delivery. We provide it under your brand, your cover page, your agency name. Your client never sees Soundcheck Insights unless you want them to.

faqs.q: What do we get at the end?
faqs.a: Two deliverables: a full In-Depth Viability Report (40–60+ pages, .docx, white-labeled) and an Executive Presentation for leadership or board conversations. Both are delivered within 14 days. One revision round is included.

expansionReport.principlesSub: Six operating principles govern every report we produce. These aren't aspirational. They're enforced at every stage of generation, review, and delivery.

principles.title: Decision-grade, not forensic
principles.desc: Public sources and lightweight proxies for 80/20 answers. Confidence labeled on every major claim: HIGH, MED, or LOW.

principles.title: Evidence first
principles.desc: Every market claim requires a data point, benchmark, or precedent with source name and date. Primary and official sources preferred.

principles.title: MECE structure
principles.desc: No filler. No repetition. Each sentence contains a new insight or substantiated fact.

principles.title: Information typing
principles.desc: Every claim tagged as FACT, ESTIMATE, or INTERPRETATION throughout the entire report.

principles.title: Model-first logic
principles.desc: Your business model is identified first. Every subsequent recommendation is calibrated to how you actually sell.

principles.title: Tariff awareness
principles.desc: If you import goods, we model current duty rates and proposed 2025-2026 tariff changes with margin scenarios.

expansionReport.pathsTitle: Every report presents three strategic paths.

paths.label: Path A
paths.name: Conservative
paths.desc: Lower-risk entry. Single channel, limited geography, slower capital burn. You learn before you invest.

paths.label: Path B
paths.name: Balanced
paths.desc: Phased multi-channel. Moderate investment over a 12-month horizon with go/no-go gates at each phase.

paths.label: Path C

paths.desc: Full-market push. Highest investment, fastest scale ambition. Maximum opportunity, maximum exposure.

expansionReport.pathsNote: The report then states which path we recommend and why, backed by 3 facts. If we recommend adjustment before entry, we specify exactly what must change and by when. Every recommendation carries an overall confidence level: HIGH, MED, or LOW, with rationale.

faqs.q: What information do you need from us to start?
faqs.a: We send you a structured intake form covering your product line, current sales and channels, target market rationale, budget range, and timeline expectations. Most clients complete it in 30 to 45 minutes. If anything is missing, we proceed using web research and proxy benchmarks, and log every assumption explicitly in the report.

faqs.q: Which markets do you cover?
faqs.a: The methodology is market-agnostic. We have delivered reports for expansion into the US, Canada, the UK, Germany, Brazil, Mexico, the UAE, and others. The report is always produced in the language of the target market and uses local currency for all financial figures.

faqs.q: How is this different from a traditional market research report?
faqs.a: Traditional reports give you data. This report gives you a decision. Every section ends with what to do, not just what we found. The CVE Score gives you a single number to anchor internal conversations. The three strategic paths force an explicit choice rather than a single consultant opinion. And the 12-month roadmap with go/no-go gates means you have a plan, not just a PDF.

faqs.q: What sources do you use?
faqs.a: We prefer primary and official sources: USDA, IRI/NIQ, Euromonitor, Census, IBISWorld, USITC, brand filings, retailer portals, and industry association reports. When official data is unavailable, we use proxies and log them explicitly in the Assumptions Log (Section 8) with confidence levels.

faqs.q: Can our agency white-label this and deliver it to our client?
faqs.a: Yes. The report is designed for white-label delivery. We provide it under your brand, your cover page, your agency name. Your client never sees Soundcheck Insights unless you want them to. This is the default for agencies and consultancies.

faqs.q: What if our client needs changes after delivery?
faqs.a: One revision round is included. If the client wants to explore a different entry path or adjust assumptions, we can update the relevant sections. Additional revision rounds are available at a flat rate.

faqs.q: How is this different from hiring an agency to run a real focus group?
faqs.a: Traditional focus groups recruit real consumers, book a facility, and run a live moderated discussion. We simulate that process using AI-generated buyer personas grounded in real market research. It's faster, cheaper, and infinitely iterable — but it's directional insight, not a replacement for primary research. Use it to narrow options before committing budget to a traditional round.

faqs.q: Where does the consumer data come from?
faqs.a: Step 1 generates three research reports from public and syndicated sources — market data, consumer behavior research, competitive intelligence. The personas in Step 2 are built from that research, not from made-up profiles. Every claim carries a source tier and confidence label.

faqs.q: Will the personas reflect my brand's actual buyers?
faqs.a: Yes — half the panel is built from your current buyer profile. The other half represents aspirational segments: people who don't buy from you today but could. That mix is what makes the feedback useful for growth, not just validation.

faqs.q: Can we re-use the same personas for multiple focus groups?
faqs.a: Yes. Once a persona panel is built, you can run unlimited focus groups against it — new concepts, new packaging, new pricing. Panels are editable, splittable, and reusable across product lines.

faqs.q: Who sees our data?
faqs.a: Only your agency tenant. Each operator gets a scoped workspace — your clients, your personas, your focus groups. Soundcheck staff can access data for support, but nothing is shared across tenants.

faqs.q: What file formats can I test?
faqs.a: Anything you can describe or upload: packaging mockups, taglines, ad concepts, product descriptions, pricing tables, campaign territories. The platform accepts images, PDFs, and text.

faqs.q: How does the feedback rework work?
faqs.a: Each session includes three rounds of iterative feedback. After reviewing the initial results, you can refine the concept — change a tagline, swap a visual, adjust a claim — and re-run the panel within the same session. No new project, no new cost. Each round delivers fresh results on the same dashboard. Additional rounds beyond three are $50 each.

faqs.q: How is this different from a growth strategy engagement?
faqs.a: Growth strategy tells you where to sell more. Scale Assessment tells you whether your operations, margins, and team can sustain 2–3× volume without breaking. It is a diagnostic before a prescription. Most brands that stall did not lack opportunities — they lacked the infrastructure to capture them durably.

faqs.q: What information do you need to start?
faqs.a: We send a structured intake covering your product lines, revenue and channel mix, team structure, current growth challenges, and strategic ambitions. Most clients complete it in 45–60 minutes. We follow up with a 2-hour stakeholder interview with leadership.

faqs.q: Can our agency white-label this?

faqs.q: What does the AI-Augmented Intelligence Layer include?
faqs.a: 90 days of automated market monitoring after report delivery: competitor movements, category signals, social listening synthesis, and pricing shifts relevant to your segment. Delivered as a monthly digest plus real-time alerts for material changes.

faqs.q: What sources do you use?
faqs.a: Primary and official sources preferred: IRI/NIQ, Euromonitor, Census, IBISWorld, brand filings, retailer data, and industry reports. When official data is unavailable, we use proxies and log them with confidence levels.

faqs.q: What is the Too Small To Fall framework?
faqs.a: Too Small To Fall is the thesis from Valter Klug's book: durable, lean, AI-augmented businesses outlast competitors who chase growth at all costs. The Scale Assessment operationalizes that thesis — identifying whether a brand is structurally built for sustainable scale or just built for revenue growth.

faqs.q: Do I need to complete the full market research before running a journey map?
faqs.a: Yes. Customer Journey Maps are built from your market research data and persona panel. Without research, the journey would be a generic category map — not brand-specific. If you haven't run research yet, start at /market-research.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a persona and a journey map?
faqs.a: A persona tells you who your buyer is — their motivations, behaviors, and decision triggers. A journey map tells you how that specific persona moves through the full purchase sequence, and where your brand is present or absent along the way. Personas answer 'who.' Journey maps answer 'how they buy.'

faqs.q: What's the difference between a journey map and a virtual focus group session?
faqs.a: A journey map shows a behavioral and temporal sequence — how a persona moves from discovery to loyalty over time. A focus group tests a specific stimulus (packaging, tagline, concept) and captures immediate reactions. Journey maps are strategic planning tools. Focus groups are testing and validation tools. They complement each other.

faqs.q: Can I re-run a journey map if my channel strategy changes?
faqs.a: Yes. Duplicate the existing journey, update the brand intake answers, and run a new version. Both versions are stored independently with timestamps.

faqs.q: How long does it take to generate a journey map?
faqs.a: The brand intake takes approximately 15 minutes to complete. Generation takes 3–5 minutes after you click Run. Total time from start to deliverable: under 25 minutes.

faqItems.q: Do I need to pay anything upfront?
faqItems.a: No. There is no setup fee for Founding Operators. You pay only the platform cost per product, per project, when you deliver. No subscription, no minimum commitment, no upfront investment.

Your founding rate is frozen at today's standard pricing and locked permanently after onboarding. Not for a contract term. Not until a pricing review. When standard rates increase in the future, your platform cost stays the same. Only this first cohort gets this lock.

faqItems.q: What if I do not have a client ready right now?
faqItems.a: You should have one in mind, even if not confirmed yet. The Founding Cohort is designed for operators who will deliver their first engagement within 60-90 days of joining. If you are more exploratory, consider applying for a future cohort when you have a real project.

faqItems.q: Do my clients see Soundcheck's brand?
faqItems.a: No. Everything is white-label from the moment you generate it. Your client sees your brand, your cover page, your agency name on the deliverable. Soundcheck is the infrastructure. You are the intelligence partner.

faqItems.q: How much time does each engagement take?
faqItems.a: About 5 hours of your time total. ~1 hour for the client intake, and ~4 hours validating the research output with your professional judgment. The platform generates the full research base in under 24 hours. The 14-day delivery timeline gives you legroom to manage multiple projects.

faqItems.q: What kind of support do I get?
faqItems.a: Direct access to Valter Klug (founder, Operator Zero) for your first two engagements. That means hands-on guidance through intake, validation, and delivery. Plus cohort peer group access and a dedicated onboarding process.

faqItems.q: Can I set my own pricing?
faqItems.a: Yes. You charge your client whatever the work is worth. Your platform cost is fixed per product. Everything above that cost is yours. Many operators add a strategy markup or bundle Soundcheck deliverables into larger engagements.

faqItems.q: How is this different from a Trial tier?
faqItems.a: Trial operators pay a higher platform cost per project (about 17% above standard) and are limited to 2 projects before graduating to Standard. Founding Operators start at 1/3 of the standard cost with zero setup, move to half during onboarding, then lock 20% below standard for life. The Founding Cohort is a significantly better deal, and it comes with founder access and hands-on support that Trial does not include.
